name: Affirm Holdings, Inc.
moat_justification: A real two-sided network with rented distribution — merchants and consumers both multi-home, the biggest partners are non-exclusive and have switched before (Walmart to Klarna), funding is wholesale rather than deposits, and the credit book has never been through a deep recession.
fragility_flags: DILUTION: share count growing 5.7%/yr — already deducted via the growth adjustment; check SBC trend
NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE: net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2024, 2025, 2026 — find the one-off (tax deposits, impairments, WC swings) before trusting the OE base
SECTOR_MODEL_MISMATCH: Finance sector — OE/capex DCF fits finance names poorly; grade confidence low
BASE_DIVERGENCE: latest FY OE/share 1.97 vs 3-yr median 0.82 — one of them is distorted; find out which and why
LOW_OE_YIELD: base OE yield 1.2% — valuation rests almost entirely on growth; tier is fragile
WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD: super-bull IV is 4.3x super-bear IV — uncertainty is huge; confidence should not be high
HIGH_NET_DEBT: net debt is 28.5x normalized OE — levered OE can vanish fast; stress the bear cases
one_liner: Fast-growing BNPL lender, moat 5/10, real profitability inflection — but at $70.10 the price assumes the inflection is permanent: weighted IRR 6.3% on the normalized base (10.7% even on the latest-FY base), IV@15% $17.70 vs $70.10; clears 15% only in the low $40s at best.
moat_for: Two-sided network at scale — 571K merchants, $50.2B FY2026 GMV, merchant net expansion ~120%
Checkout distribution rivals must displace — Amazon through Jan 2031, Shopify, Apple Pay
Underwriting data advantage at >$50B/yr GMV; interest-bearing mix monetizes better than Klarna's
Affirm Card: 5.2M cardholders, doubled YoY, raises consumer switching friction
moat_against: Distribution is rented and non-exclusive — Walmart shifted primary BNPL to Klarna
Klarna, PayPal, Block/Afterpay and card issuers all compete; consumers multi-home
No deposit funding — warehouse/securitization at ~5.8% cost of funds, can reprice or close
Credit book untested through a deep recession; delinquencies and provisions rising
